links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of reasoning models versus their base models on the same cases
links.effect: R1-671B beat DeepSeek-V3 (95.45% vs 88.18%; p=0.008); R1-8B underperformed Llama3.1-8B (47.27% vs 64.54%; p=0.003); no significant differences for mid-sized models.
links.quote: The study concludes that the DeepSeek-R1-671B shows potential for medical diagnosis, but distilled models do not exceed their base models.

links.outcome: Error modes in chain-of-thought for incorrect diagnostic cases, including diagnostic priority inversion
links.effect: Three error modes prevalent across distilled models: reasoning drift, red-flag recognition failure, and diagnostic priority inversion (qualitative; no counts reported).
links.quote: Qualitative analysis of the chain-of-thought outputs in incorrect cases revealed three universally prevalent error modes across distilled models: Reasoning drift, Red-Flag recognition failure, and diagnostic priority inversion.

links.outcome: Recognition of red-flag (serious) findings in incorrect diagnostic cases
links.effect: Red-flag recognition failure was one of three universally prevalent error modes in distilled models' incorrect cases (qualitative; no counts reported).
links.quote: Qualitative analysis of the chain-of-thought outputs in incorrect cases revealed three universally prevalent error modes across distilled models: Reasoning drift, Red-Flag recognition failure, and diagnostic priority inversion.

screen.reason: Evaluates diagnostic performance and error modes of DeepSeek-R1 distilled and base models on simulated clinical case benchmarks without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
